You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Validus Holdings, Ltd. (acquired business) realized record after acquisition by AIG, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the acquired entity deregistered its
> securities and ceased separate public reporting, there is no post-closing public
> 10-K/20-F for Validus itself; this sub-dossier instead checks whether the acquirer
> (American International Group, Inc., CIK 0000005272) separately discloses the
> acquired business's own trajectory in its subsequent Forms 10-K. This sub-dossier
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured or negotiated.

## Public-reporting status through the outcome window
- The acquired entity does not file periodic reports on its own account: its last
  annual report on Form 10-K covered fiscal year 2017 (filed February 28, 2018,
  pre-closing); no subsequent Form 10-K, 10-K/A, or 20-F was filed under CIK 0001348259. [SRC: SEC accession 0001348259-18-000008, Form 10-K FY2017 (last annual filing on this CIK)]
- A search of the acquirer's (AIG, CIK 0000005272) Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021
  (filed February 17, 2022 — within the ~3-5-year outcome window) finds Validus
  referenced only as an operating-company name and a debt-schedule line item within
  AIG's consolidated "General Insurance" segment; no standalone revenue, earnings,
  premium volume, or profitability figures are broken out for Validus, Validus
  Reinsurance, Talbot, Western World, or AlphaCat individually anywhere in that filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-22-024701, AIG Form 10-K FY2021]

## What IS disclosed about the acquired business within AIG's consolidated filings
- AIG's FY2021 Form 10-K lists Validus Reinsurance, Ltd. (Validus Re), Talbot Holdings
  Ltd. (Talbot), and Western World Insurance Group, Inc. among the "major operating
  companies" comprising its General Insurance segment (alongside National Union,
  American Home, Lexington, and other legacy AIG entities), indicating the acquired
  businesses continued to operate under their pre-acquisition names as constituent
  units of AIG's General Insurance segment as of that filing date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-22-024701, AIG Form 10-K FY2021, "Business" — segment description]
- AIG's FY2021 Form 10-K discloses "Validus notes and bonds payable" as a distinct
  line item within AIG's general-borrowings debt schedule, at a carrying amount of
  $293 million as of December 31, 2021 versus $348 million as of December 31, 2020,
  bearing a stated rate of 8.88% and maturing in 2040; this is a debt-schedule
  disclosure, not an earnings or revenue disclosure for the acquired business. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-22-024701, AIG Form 10-K FY2021, Note on Long-Term Debt / Enterprise Risk Management debt-maturity table]
- Validus Reinsurance, Ltd. is separately named in AIG's catastrophe-reinsurance risk
  disclosure (e.g., a described program of catastrophe protection including $400
  million of per-occurrence limit in excess of a $150 million retention for named
  windstorm outside North America), consistent with Validus Re continuing to operate
  as an active reinsurance underwriting entity within AIG's structure. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-22-024701, AIG Form 10-K FY2021, Item 7 "Enterprise Risk Management"]
- Financial-strength ratings for Validus Reinsurance, Ltd. are listed separately
  alongside AIG's other insurance operating subsidiaries (rated A / A+ / -- / A2 by the
  agencies shown), again without an accompanying standalone financial-performance
  disclosure. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-22-024701, AIG Form 10-K FY2021, "Ratings" table]
- AIG's goodwill/intangible-asset note states that "Other intangible assets and Value
  of distribution network acquired (VODA) resulted primarily from the acquisition of
  Validus," but the accompanying roll-forward table presents these balances at the
  consolidated segment level (not isolated to a Validus-only figure), so no
  Validus-specific dollar impairment or write-down figure can be extracted from this
  disclosure. [UNVERIFIED — figure not separately attributable to Validus]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable in this pass
- No divestiture, dissolution, or separate wind-down of the acquired business was
  identified in the reviewed filing; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence
  given the lack of standalone reporting, so this is not coded as a confirmed
  "no divestiture" outcome. [UNVERIFIED]
- No AIG segment disclosure isolating Validus's own revenue, net income/loss, loss
  ratio, or premium volume was located in the reviewed FY2021 Form 10-K. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The acquired entity (Validus Holdings, Ltd.) ceased separate public reporting after
  its acquisition closed and has no subsequent Form 10-K or 20-F of its own; the
  acquirer's (AIG's) FY2021 Form 10-K confirms the acquired operating companies
  (Validus Re, Talbot, Western World) continued to operate under their own names within
  AIG's consolidated General Insurance segment and discloses only a debt-schedule line
  item (assumed Validus notes/bonds payable, declining from $348 million at year-end
  2020 to $293 million at year-end 2021) and ratings/risk-program mentions for the
  acquired entities — no standalone revenue, earnings, or profitability trajectory for
  the acquired business is separately disclosed. Per the no-public-record convention,
  the realized 3-5-year outcome for this business is coded **uncertain**: the public
  record does not permit an independent assessment of the acquired business's own
  post-acquisition performance trajectory. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-22-024701, AIG Form 10-K FY2021]

[SLICE END]
